summary: POWERGRID builds and runs the long-distance electricity lines and substations that connect power stations with places needing power.
description: Electricity produced at a power station has to travel before it reaches a home or factory. POWERGRID supplies part of that route: high-voltage lines move power over long distances, and substations connect and control parts of the network, including changing voltage where needed. Local distribution networks then serve customers.
money: Electricity companies pay for its network to be available to carry power under the relevant agreements and pricing rules. The group also earns from helping plan electricity networks and providing fibre connections. It pays to build and maintain lines and substations, employ people and fund borrowing. A proposed power line is different from one that has been built, tested and put into service.
customers: Distribution companies and other electricity-sector users pay network charges under the applicable arrangements. POWERGRID usually does not send a household its local electricity bill. Businesses buying telecom connections or advisory work pay under separate service contracts.
drivers: Completion of projects, the agreed or approved network charge, whether equipment remains ready to carry power, construction and maintenance costs, borrowing costs and customer payment.

groups.title: Long-distance electricity transmission
groups.examples: High-voltage lines, substations and connections between regions.
groups.explanation: These provide a route for electricity rather than making it. The network has to be connected, controlled and maintained so power can move where required under the electricity system’s operating rules.

groups.title: Specialised transmission links
groups.examples: High-voltage direct-current links and associated equipment.
groups.explanation: Direct current means electrical current flows in one direction. These links use that transmission technology for the required connection. They are still part of the transmission job, with their own equipment, construction and maintenance needs.

groups.title: Project work and consultancy
groups.examples: Engineering and relevant network planning or advisory assignments.
groups.explanation: Consultancy means a customer pays for agreed advice or technical work. Building and operating a network asset is a different commitment, involving construction money and longer-term service obligations.

groups.title: Telecom connections
groups.explanation: Optical fibre carries data using light. The group supplies relevant connectivity services alongside its electricity-network activities. The customer contract and costs differ from those of carrying power.

basics.title: A transmission charge is not a household electricity bill
basics.text: The power station earns for generating power; POWERGRID earns for the network service under its terms. The local supplier bills most households. These businesses can all be involved in electricity reaching the same customer, but they earn for different jobs.

basics.title: Readiness can matter as much as the amount carried
basics.text: Availability means equipment is ready for service. Transmission charges can depend on agreed availability conditions and pricing rules. Higher national electricity use does not automatically increase the charge on every existing line.

steps.title: Obtain a project with defined terms
steps.text: Receive the relevant assignment or win a competitive award. Read the promised completion date, charges and responsibilities.

steps.title: Arrange the route and build
steps.text: Obtain permissions to use the route, order equipment and construct lines and substations. Work must connect with the other parts of the electricity network.

steps.title: Test and bring it into service
steps.text: Commissioning means completing the required testing and bringing the asset into service. Maintain it so it remains ready to carry power.

steps.title: Bill, collect and maintain the network
steps.text: Collect charges under the applicable arrangement while paying maintenance, staff and borrowing costs and funding further projects.

specifics.title: Spending on a line is different from having an earning line
specifics.text: Capital work in progress means money spent on assets not yet ready for their intended use. A line may still need equipment, permissions, tests or a connection. Delays can postpone income while costs continue.

specifics.title: An approved charge and a competitive bid work differently
specifics.text: For a regulated project, the pricing authority reviews the relevant costs and rules when setting charges. In a competitively bid project, the promised charge and contract matter. Neither route means every cost overrun is automatically paid by customers.

specifics.title: A reliable line can still have poor economics
specifics.text: Keeping the network ready is necessary, but construction cost and borrowing terms also matter. A project that costs much more than planned may leave less after costs even when the equipment works well.

watch: Are projects becoming working connections on time?
A new award is future work, not a completed service.
Check the construction schedule, tests and commissioning. Read whether connected power stations or other lines must also be ready before the project can be useful and earn under its terms.
What can the project charge customers?
The agreement controls which costs and returns can be recovered.
Identify whether charges are set through regulatory review or competitive bidding. Read availability conditions, disputed costs and later changes rather than assuming a standard guaranteed return.
Is equipment remaining ready for service?
Faults and outages can affect charges and add repair costs.
Read availability, unexpected outages and maintenance. Check any rewards or deductions linked to performance, with the period and assets covered.
Does new construction justify the money committed?
More spending is not itself more income.

Compare investment still under construction with completed assets, later income, cash from operations and borrowing costs. Read when investment moves from construction into assets ready for use; distinguish this from starting construction.
Are customers paying, and which business is being measured?
Unpaid bills and group-company changes can alter the picture.

Check money customers owe and payments collected. Keep transmission, telecom and consultancy distinct, and do not mix the parent’s standalone accounts with consolidated accounts covering controlled companies.
risks: Permissions to use land, equipment supply or delays in connected projects can postpone service.
Allowed charges or bid costs disappoint
A pricing decision or an overly costly project can reduce what remains after costs.
Equipment faults, severe weather and other outages can interrupt availability and require repairs.
Late customer payments and borrowing costs can squeeze funds while construction continues.
context: Two renewable-power routes won in 2026 are still years from service

A solar or wind farm needs lines and substations to send its power to buyers. POWERGRID’s 4 August 2026 release says it won two such projects through tariff-based competitive bidding, where companies compete on the charge they would collect for building and running the line. Winning meant taking over a special purpose vehicle (SPV), a company set up for one project, from the government agency running the bid. Bhadla Ramgarh Power Transmission will add equipment at existing substations in Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh and is scheduled for commissioning, meaning testing and bringing into service, by 20 January 2029. Krishnagiri REZ Transmission will build two new substations and lines across Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka within 36 months. POWERGRID will build, own and run these assets for the contract period and later hand them over. Until they are working, they need construction money but do not yet earn their charges.
quiz: Does POWERGRID usually make the electricity carried by its transmission lines?

Its main transmission job is to carry power through a network. Generating stations produce it, and local distribution companies take it towards users. Check the specific business rather than treating them as the same job.

financialNotes.title: Commissioned assets and profit are different measures
financialNotes.text: Use the reporting scope and earnings definition printed with the audited figures. Transmission charges, other business income and group profit are different measures. Regulated tariff calculations and system capacity do not substitute for recognised income, operating cash or the cost of funding new projects.
